source.modification: Removed three automatic fsck_hfs commands from restored_external, retaining partition readiness checks, USB initialization, kernel boot arguments and original read-only data mounting. Added a strict decimal --sleep SECONDS mode (0..3600) which returns before hardware initialization and resumes interrupted libc sleep calls. Verify the HFS root's device number against the /dev/md0 block device, accepting XNU's initial root_device label. Skip an already writable root; otherwise use a checked mount(2) update with the pinned XNU HFS arguments to avoid mount_hfs reopening the mounted RAM device. Disable stdout buffering at the start of the recovery program so progress reaches the display wrapper immediately; no recovery algorithm changes.

verification.imports: all imported symbols matched to actual iPhone1,2 4.2.1 8C148 restore ramdisk ARMv6 libraries
verification.code_signatures: codesign --verify --strict and independent SHA1/SHA256 code page hashing
verification.automatic_filesystem_repair: All three fsck_hfs invocations removed from restored_external; command absent from final binary; partition wait and USB initialization retained.
verification.bounded_wait_helper: The exact helper passed native-host argument, bounds, overflow and interrupted-sleep tests. Its ARMv6 --sleep 1 path completed successfully on the phone, and --sleep 3601 returned the expected usage error before hardware initialization.
verification.hardware_scope: The rebuilt restored_external ran in a diagnostic 4.2.1 RAM disk on the owner's iPhone1,2 through an Apple Silicon MacBook. Authenticated SSH/SFTP verified its SHA-256 and a writable /dev/md0 root with only devfs alongside it. The passcode-recovery and device_infos executables were not executed.
verification.console_output: The exact stdio helper passed a harmless native-host C test through the real display wrapper: progress arrived before process exit; a control without the helper reproduced buffering. The rebuilt recovery executable has not been executed on a phone.
